law: tech#12 (P2 queue R1827). S2 asr-check QC channel, OPT-IN ONLY (--noise-dict). NEVER for real-voice transcripts (persona rule: real voice first - corrupting a real-voice transcript with a TTS-domain dictionary is forbidden).
direction: noise -> true : noise = what the ASR channel wrote, true = the term the TTS track actually says (evidence-anchored, zero invention)
evidence: docs/reviews/station-reviews.md asr-check rows: BS-002 R174 / BS-003 R180 / BS-004 R187 / BS-013 R1683 / BS-014 R1686 / BS-015 R1690 / BS-016 R1693

classes.safe: noise string is implausible in the production domain; fires unconditionally when the dict is on
classes.guarded: noise string is a plausible/common word; fires ONLY when the --expect reference text (the piece's own beats) contains the true term (collision guard)
classes.excluded: observed but deliberately NOT in the auto table: single-char over-broad pairs, unstable long-span garble, tail-silence hallucination, traditional-variant glyphs (see excluded[])

verdict: dictionary suppression is VIABLE and low-risk under three gates: (1) opt-in flag only, default off; (2) guarded entries require --expect (the piece's own beats) so a common-word noise never fires when the true term is absent; (3) single-char and garble families stay out (they are model-quality faces, not dictionary faces). Covered classes = stable homophone pairs recurring across pieces (日志/在册/板块 hook/档->大/推演声明族).
